get.description: Interactive API documentation interface using Swagger UI
Retrieve the OpenAPI 3.0 specification in JSON format for this API

metadata.description: Arbitrary structured data that stores information about the log - e.g., userId: 100.

valid.description: Valid is true if Time is not NULL

error.description:
Error is the stable human-readable message. Always
"Operation is already running" — kept for backwards
compatibility with clients that key off the error string.

job_id.description:
JobID is the opaque identifier of the currently-running job.
Clients can pass this straight to CancelOperationJob or
GetOperationJobStatus. Empty only for legacy holders that have
not migrated to the JobManager.Begin path yet.

kind.description:
Kind is the operation kind holding the lock. One of "pull",
"push", "patch", "schema". Helps operators distinguish a
long-running pull from a fast sync push when triaging
contention.

operation_id.description:
OperationID is the connector-service-local numeric ID of the
operation the lock was taken on. Present so operator-facing
logs can cross-reference the operation row directly.

started_at.description:
StartedAt is when the in-flight job was accepted. Clients can
compute elapsed time to decide whether to wait or cancel. nil
for legacy sync holders with no registered row.

Pointer rather than time.Time + omitempty because encoding/json's
omitempty does not treat a zero time.Time as empty — it would
serialise as "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z" on the wire. Matches the
convention used by ExpiresAt above and the *time.Time fields
in the other models in this package.

authorization_url.description:
AuthorizationURL is the user-agent-facing endpoint where the end
user approves the connection. Absolute https:// URL.

dcr_endpoint.description:
DCREndpoint is optional (RFC 7591). When set, the Core can
dynamically register an OAuth client per workspace on first use,
skipping the need for an admin-configured app. MCP-compatible
vendors (Intercom, Linear, Sentry, ...) typically provide this.

extra_params.description:
ExtraParams are vendor-specific parameters appended to the
authorization request (e.g., access_type=offline, prompt=consent).
Keys that would override security-critical OAuth params are
silently dropped by the Core.

pkce.description:
PKCE must be true for new connectors. The Core refuses to run a
flow when this is false. Retained as a field (rather than an
always-true default) so the contract is explicit on the wire.

provider.description:
Provider is a short canonical identifier for the vendor, e.g.
"hubspot", "stripe", "intercom". Used in logs + error messages.

revocation_url.description:
RevocationURL is optional (RFC 7009). When set, the Core POSTs the
token here on disconnect so the vendor drops the grant immediately.

scopes.description:
Scopes is the set of OAuth scopes the connector declares it needs.
Read-only by default; connectors should follow least-privilege.

token_url.description: TokenURL is the token endpoint (RFC 6749 §3.2). Absolute https:// URL.

userinfo_url.description:
UserinfoURL is optional. When set, the Core may call it after a
successful exchange to populate a friendly "connected as <who>"
label in the UI. Not used in the Phase 2 wiring; reserved.

can_connect.description: Indicates if the connector can connect to the external system

connection_details_valid.description: Indicates if the connection details are valid

connection_settings_valid.description: Indicates if the connection settings are valid

ok.description: Indicates if the configuration is valid

has_more.description: HasMore indicates if there are more items available

next.description: Next is the next page number or token, if applicable

total.description: Total is the total number of items available

properties.description: Properties of the schema, formatted like {"name":{"type":"string"},"age":{"type":"integer"}}

x-original-duckdb-type.description: Extension fields for metadata and traceability

error.description:
Error is the operator-facing human-readable message. Stable
enough for log grep but not a machine-readable code.

job_id.description:
JobID echoes the ID from the URL when the server could parse
one. Empty for request-level failures (malformed URL, missing
path parameter).

reason.description:
Reason is the machine-readable failure classification. See
JobErrorReason for the stable value set.

retryable.description:
Retryable reports whether the caller should retry the same
request after a short backoff. False for any terminal failure
mode (not_found, corrupted_job_state, invalid_request).

description.example: Customer data in JSON format with contact information

restrictions.description: Restrictions are not required, but are available for group schemas

job_id.description:
JobID is the identifier the caller uses on subsequent
/operation/status and /operation/result calls.

operation_token.description:
OperationToken is the per-job bearer credential for lifecycle
routes. Minted by the server on Start*; TTL matches the
underlying OperationJob row.

connection_oauth_config.description:
ConnectionOAuthConfig is optional. When set, the connector declares
it uses OAuth 2.0 (authorization code + PKCE) for authenticating a
Connection, and Irmin Core runs the flow on the user's behalf. Nil
means the connector uses the legacy DynamicField form path
(password / API key / etc.). See OAUTH-CONNECTORS.md for the flow
+ patterns + which vendors are planned.
